  - [19:05:24–19:07:04] **Managing Data Intermediaries: Primary vs Direct Responsibility**

    One more administrative measure is managing data intermediaries. You'll recall that in the second seminar we talked about the concept of a data intermediary. There can be a data controller–data intermediary relationship, where the data intermediary processes personal data on behalf of the data controller. For example, if you engage Microsoft for cloud storage, Microsoft is a data intermediary. We also talked about how, in general, the data intermediary is not bound by most of the PDPA's obligations, because it is not the data controller. That's what I mentioned in that seminar. But the thing to understand, as far as the Protection Obligation is concerned, is that both parties are responsible. The Protection Obligation is one of those obligations that hits both the controller and the intermediary.

    Looking at it from the controller's perspective, one of the things the controller has to do is govern its data intermediaries, and that's also an important security measure. Of course, this only applies if you are appointing an intermediary. So how does the PDPC look at this kind of relationship? What it has said in some cases is that the data controller has the so-called "primary" responsibility for security, whereas the data intermediary has the "direct" responsibility.

    还有一项行政措施是管理数据中介（data intermediary）。你们应该记得，在第二次研讨课上我们讲过数据中介的概念。可以存在数据控制者与数据中介的关系，即数据中介代表数据控制者处理个人数据。例如，如果你聘请微软提供云存储，微软就是数据中介。我们也讲过，一般而言，数据中介不受 PDPA 大部分义务的约束，因为它不是数据控制者。这是我在那次研讨课上提到的。但就保护义务而言，你需要理解的是，双方都负有责任。保护义务是同时约束控制者和中介的义务之一。

    从控制者的角度来看，控制者必须做的事情之一就是管理其数据中介，这也是一项重要的安全措施。当然，这只适用于你委任了中介的情况。那么 PDPC 如何看待这种关系？它在一些案例中说过，数据控制者对安全负有所谓的"首要"责任，而数据中介负有"直接"责任。

  - [19:07:32–19:10:23] **Both Parties in Breach: The Cellar Door (2016)**

    The Cellar Door case illustrates this point. The data controller here is The Cellar Door, which sells various food, wine, beverages, and so on. It appointed GIW, an IT service provider, to build its website and host its data. Then in 2014, it was discovered that The Cellar Door's customer data had been leaked and uploaded onto Pastebin, which is a place where hackers tend to upload their materials. Both parties were unable to figure out how the data got leaked. The PDPC investigated and found that both The Cellar Door, as the controller, and GIW, as the intermediary, were in breach.

    So how does the PDPC look at this scenario? First, it concludes that GIW is the intermediary, because it is processing customer data on behalf of The Cellar Door. The processing takes place because GIW was hosting, or storing, The Cellar Door's customer data, and that counts as processing. So now you have this relationship. What is the data controller supposed to do? As the data controller, The Cellar Door has the so-called primary responsibility. What that means is that the controller's responsibility is to put in place security measures that the intermediary is supposed to follow. For example, the controller should make sure that in its contract with the intermediary, security arrangements are imposed. It may also need to follow up with checks to make sure the intermediary is actually following through on whatever security arrangements were agreed. So that's primary responsibility. As for the intermediary, which has the direct responsibility, that's more straightforward: the intermediary needs to carry out whatever security arrangements were agreed. In this case, both organisations failed in their respective responsibilities.

    The Cellar Door 案说明了这一点。这里的数据控制者是 The Cellar Door，销售各种食品、葡萄酒、饮料等。它委任了 IT 服务商 GIW 为其建网站并托管数据。到了 2014 年，人们发现 The Cellar Door 的客户数据被泄露并上传到了 Pastebin，那是黑客常常上传他们材料的地方。双方都没能查明数据是如何泄露的。PDPC 调查后认定，作为控制者的 The Cellar Door 和作为中介的 GIW 都违反了义务。

    那么 PDPC 是如何分析这个情形的？首先，它认定 GIW 是中介，因为它代表 The Cellar Door 处理客户数据。之所以构成处理，是因为 GIW 托管、即存储了 The Cellar Door 的客户数据，这就算处理。于是就有了这种关系。那么数据控制者应该做什么？作为数据控制者，The Cellar Door 负有所谓的首要责任。这意味着，控制者的责任是制定中介需要遵守的安全措施。例如，控制者应确保在与中介的合同中规定安全安排。它可能还需要跟进检查，确保中介确实落实了所约定的安全安排。这就是首要责任。至于负有直接责任的中介，那就更直接了：中介需要执行所约定的任何安全安排。在这个案例中，两个组织都没有履行各自的责任。

  - [19:10:23–19:13:53] **Controller Compliant, Intermediary in Breach: Singapore Telecommunications (2017)**

    From this point, you can already see that it is possible for one party to succeed but the other to fail. There will be some cases where the data intermediary, because of their carelessness, fails to comply with the Protection Obligation, but the controller is found to have done enough. So it's possible for the controller to have fulfilled its responsibility even if the intermediary fails.

    The case that highlights this point is, again, a Singtel case, an earlier one. The context is the Singtel ONEPASS service, which allowed customers to access their accounts with Singtel. Singtel engaged an intermediary called Tech Mahindra to develop and maintain this ONEPASS service. One Singtel customer complained they were having login difficulties. Singtel forwarded this complaint to Tech Mahindra, which realised it needed to update this customer's profile. So it executed a database script to update the profile. But after the script was run, it was found that other ONEPASS accounts had also been modified to show that particular user's personal data. This happened to up to 2.78 million accounts. The reason this somewhat dramatic incident happened was that when Tech Mahindra wrote the script, they forgot to add the WHERE clause, so the change affected every single customer's profile instead of just the one affected customer.

    So, data breach, the PDPC investigates, and interestingly, it found that while the intermediary, Tech Mahindra, was in breach, Singtel, the controller, was not. The reason is that Singtel did actually do what was necessary as data controller. In the contract, it required Tech Mahindra to adhere to its data security policies. It required training. It imposed an SOP requiring database changes to be done in a development environment first. It did on-site security reviews, conducted its own penetration testing, and so on. So it actually did the full suite of things a responsible data controller should do. Tech Mahindra, on the other hand, failed its direct responsibility. To put it simply, they didn't follow instructions, and that was a breach of the Protection Obligation. What this case highlights is that, as the controller, as long as you do what you're required to do, even if the intermediary fails on their side, you will not be held liable.

    从这里你已经可以看出，有可能一方合规而另一方违规。会有一些案例中，数据中介因为自己粗心而没有遵守保护义务，但控制者被认定已经尽到了责任。所以，即使中介失职，控制者也有可能已经履行了自己的责任。

    说明这一点的案例同样是 Singtel 案，一个更早的案子。背景是 Singtel 的 ONEPASS 服务，让客户访问自己在 Singtel 的账户。Singtel 委托一家叫 Tech Mahindra 的中介开发和维护 ONEPASS 服务。一位 Singtel 客户投诉登录有困难。Singtel 把投诉转给 Tech Mahindra，Tech Mahindra 发现需要更新这位客户的资料。于是它执行了一个数据库脚本来更新资料。但脚本运行后，人们发现其他 ONEPASS 账户也被修改成显示这位用户的个人数据。受影响的账户多达 278 万个。之所以发生这么戏剧性的事件，是因为 Tech Mahindra 写脚本时忘了加 WHERE 子句，导致修改影响了每一位客户的资料，而不只是那一位受影响的客户。

    于是发生了数据泄露，PDPC 进行调查，有意思的是，它认定中介 Tech Mahindra 违规，而控制者 Singtel 没有违规。原因是 Singtel 确实做了数据控制者该做的事。它在合同中要求 Tech Mahindra 遵守其数据安全政策，要求进行培训，规定了数据库变更必须先在开发环境中进行的标准作业程序（SOP），进行了现场安全审查，还自行做了渗透测试等等。所以它确实做了一个负责任的数据控制者应做的全套工作。而 Tech Mahindra 则没有履行其直接责任。简单说，他们没有按指示办事，这就违反了保护义务。这个案例说明，作为控制者，只要你做了你需要做的事，即使中介那边出了问题，你也不会被追究责任。

  - [19:14:17–19:18:35] **Reasonable Oversight Required: Fullerton Healthcare Group (2023)**

    So what are data controllers supposed to do with their data intermediaries? One thing, as we mentioned, is the need to impose certain security measures on the intermediary. It is now common practice that when you contract with a data intermediary, you make sure there are security obligations in the contract. So that's common. The more difficult question is: are you really expected to make sure the data intermediary follows through? Here, we have cases that say different things.

    One case, Fullerton Healthcare Group, suggests that you are actually expected to exercise supervision. This case is interesting. Fullerton is an enterprise healthcare service provider. Fullerton engaged Agape, a social enterprise, to provide call centre and appointment booking services. And because Agape is a social enterprise, it engaged inmates from Changi Women's Prison to provide some of these call centre services. In order for Agape to provide these services, Fullerton gave Agape access to customers' personal data. The way it did this was by authorising one Agape computer through which Agape could access Fullerton's customer data. I guess this was to make sure there was only one channel through which the data could flow. But I guess Agape didn't get the memo. What they did was download the whole database and re-upload it onto their own online drive, to allow the inmates to also access the data. Subsequently, Fullerton realised that the data was being sold on the dark web. It investigated by hiring a security consultant, who found the seller of the data, and the seller claimed to have exfiltrated the data from Agape's online drive. So that was the vulnerability.

    The PDPC found a breach of the Protection Obligation on both sides, the controller and the intermediary. Focusing on the controller, Fullerton, the PDPC said that organisations should exercise, quote unquote, "reasonable oversight" over their data intermediaries. Fullerton did do some things. It carried out due diligence on Agape and imposed the usual security measures in the contract. So it did the basic things. But it did not exercise reasonable oversight by monitoring how Agape was handling the personal data. Specifically, the PDPC said that since Fullerton was aware that Agape was engaging prison inmates to carry out the services, it should have asked how exactly Agape was planning to give the inmates access. If it had asked those questions, it would probably have stepped in to stop this download-and-re-upload process. So this was a case where the PDPC said the controller was expected to supervise.

    那么，数据控制者应该如何对待其数据中介？如前所述，其中一件事是需要对中介施加某些安全措施。现在的普遍做法是，与数据中介签合同时，确保合同中有安全义务。这很常见。更难的问题是：你是否真的需要确保数据中介切实执行？在这一点上，不同案例的说法不一样。

    其中一个案例，Fullerton Healthcare Group（富乐顿医疗集团）案，表明你确实需要进行监督。这个案子很有意思。Fullerton 是一家企业医疗服务提供商。Fullerton 聘请了社会企业 Agape 提供呼叫中心和预约服务。由于 Agape 是社会企业，它雇用了樟宜女子监狱的囚犯来提供部分呼叫中心服务。为了让 Agape 提供这些服务，Fullerton 向 Agape 提供了客户个人数据的访问权限。具体方式是授权 Agape 的一台电脑访问 Fullerton 的客户数据。我想这是为了确保数据只通过一个渠道流动。但我猜 Agape 没收到这个通知。他们把整个数据库下载下来，再重新上传到自己的在线云盘，好让囚犯也能访问数据。后来，Fullerton 发现这些数据正在暗网上出售。它聘请了安全顾问进行调查，顾问找到了数据卖家，卖家声称他是从 Agape 的在线云盘中窃取的数据。这就是漏洞所在。

    PDPC 认定控制者和中介双方都违反了保护义务。就控制者 Fullerton 而言，PDPC 说组织应当对其数据中介进行所谓的"合理监督"。Fullerton 确实做了一些事情：它对 Agape 做了尽职调查，并在合同中规定了常规的安全措施。所以基本的事情它做了。但它没有通过监控 Agape 如何处理个人数据来进行合理监督。具体而言，PDPC 认为，既然 Fullerton 知道 Agape 雇用囚犯来提供服务，它就应该询问 Agape 究竟打算如何让囚犯获得访问权限。如果它问了这些问题，它很可能就会介入，阻止这种下载再上传的做法。所以在这个案例中，PDPC 认为控制者有监督的义务。

  - [19:18:43–19:20:41] **No Supervision Required: AIG Asia Pacific Insurance (2019)**

    But you also have other cases where the PDPC says you don't have to supervise. For example, in the AIG case, you have an insurance company that contracted with an intermediary called Toppan to print and mail letters. In one instance, Toppan sent out a batch of renewal letters for motor insurance. These letters contained a form with customer information for customers who wanted to renew their insurance, plus a business reply envelope, so that customers, after filling in the form, could put it into the envelope and send it back. In this instance, one of Toppan's employees, when packing the letters, inserted the wrong business reply envelopes. So if a customer filled in the form and used that envelope, the form would go to another company, Tan Chong Credit.

    The PDPC said there was a breach of the Protection Obligation, but not by AIG; AIG was okay. The PDPC noted that AIG did put in place contractual requirements for Toppan to secure personal data, including when packing these letters. And although AIG didn't actually supervise how the mailing was done, the PDPC said it was not reasonable to expect AIG to supervise that, in particular because of Toppan's credibility and reputation. I'm not sure whether Toppan does in fact have such a reputation, but that was what the PDPC decided.

    但也有其他案例中，PDPC 认为你不需要监督。例如在 AIG 案中，一家保险公司与一家叫 Toppan（凸版）的中介签约，由其打印和邮寄信件。有一次，Toppan 寄出了一批汽车保险续保信。这些信件里有一份包含客户信息的表格，供想要续保的客户填写，另外附有一个商业回邮信封，客户填好表格后可以装进信封寄回。这一次，Toppan 的一名员工在装信时放错了商业回邮信封。所以如果客户填好表格并使用那个信封，表格就会寄到另一家公司陈振中信贷（Tan Chong Credit）。

    PDPC 认定存在违反保护义务的情况，但违规的不是 AIG，AIG 没有问题。PDPC 指出，AIG 确实在合同中要求 Toppan 保护个人数据，包括在装封这些信件时。虽然 AIG 并没有实际监督邮寄过程，但 PDPC 认为期望 AIG 去监督这一点是不合理的，尤其是考虑到 Toppan 的信誉和声誉。我不确定 Toppan 是否真的有这样的声誉，但这就是 PDPC 的决定。

  - [19:20:41–19:24:55] **Discussion: Why Supervise in Fullerton but Not in AIG?**

    So one question we might consider is whether there are any relevant differences between the AIG case and the Fullerton case. What makes it so that in one case you must supervise, but in the other case you don't have to?

    A student suggests two differences: first, the quality of the intermediary; second, whether or not you know they are engaging inmates.

    So one differentiating factor is that in the AIG case you had an intermediary that was more credible. Agape was probably a newer sort of player, and it was doing this interesting arrangement of engaging prison inmates. Any other relevant differences?

    Another student points to the access arrangement: in Fullerton, you'd only need to ask some more questions about how the intermediary was giving access to the data; whereas in AIG, knowing the process would require actually going down to watch, which would take too much effort.

    So another differentiating factor is that in the Fullerton case, supervision was actually quite simple, because Fullerton just had to ask the right question. Whereas supervision in the AIG case was much more onerous. You'd almost have to send someone down, twenty-four seven, to watch them do the work, in which case you might as well do it yourself. I think in cases where supervision would involve an unreasonable amount of effort, you cannot reasonably be expected to do it.

    One more distinguishing factor you can see is that in the Fullerton case the data is fairly sensitive, because it involves at least some health information and financial information. Whereas in the motor insurance case, it's probably not that sensitive.

    A student asks: couldn't AIG have asked Toppan how they prevent accidental swapping of the letters and envelopes? Wouldn't that be a similar question to the one Fullerton should have asked?

    I think asking a question in this case would not change anything, because AIG did impose contractual requirements for Toppan to take care when sending out these letters. I suppose it is possible they could have asked further questions about the specific procedures when packing the letters into the envelopes. But I think the PDPC used the word "micromanagement" in relation to that. It took the view that you could not reasonably expect AIG to micromanage that. Whereas in the Fullerton case, the question to be asked was a fairly broad one: essentially, how are you giving access, and how do you intend to achieve it?

    所以我们可以思考一个问题：AIG 案和 Fullerton 案之间有没有相关的区别？为什么一个案子中你必须监督，而另一个案子中你不必？

    一位同学提出两点区别：第一，中介的素质；第二，你是否知道他们雇用了囚犯。

    所以一个区分因素是，在 AIG 案中，中介更有信誉。Agape 可能是个较新的参与者，而且它采用了雇用囚犯这种很特别的安排。还有其他相关区别吗？

    另一位同学指出访问安排的问题：在 Fullerton 案中，你只需要多问几个关于中介如何提供数据访问的问题；而在 AIG 案中，要了解流程就需要实际去现场看，这会耗费太多精力。

    所以另一个区分因素是，在 Fullerton 案中，监督其实相当简单，Fullerton 只需要问对问题就行。而在 AIG 案中，监督要繁重得多。你几乎需要派人去现场，全天候盯着他们干活，那样的话你还不如自己做。我认为，在监督需要付出不合理程度精力的情况下，不能合理地期望你去做。

    你还能看到另一个区分因素：在 Fullerton 案中，数据相当敏感，因为至少涉及一些健康信息和财务信息。而在汽车保险的案子里，数据可能没那么敏感。

    一位同学问：AIG 难道不能问问 Toppan 他们如何防止信件和信封被意外装错吗？这不就和 Fullerton 本该问的问题类似吗？

    我认为在这个案子里问这个问题不会改变什么，因为 AIG 确实在合同中要求 Toppan 在寄送这些信件时谨慎处理。我想他们确实有可能进一步询问装信封时的具体流程。但我记得 PDPC 在这一点上用了"微观管理（micromanagement）"这个词。它认为不能合理地期望 AIG 去微观管理这种事情。而在 Fullerton 案中，需要问的问题是一个相当宽泛的问题：本质上就是，你们如何提供访问权限，打算怎么实现？

Because if you expect Singtel to review every single code change this particular vendor makes, that might require so much effort that it would no longer be worthwhile appointing the vendor. So I'm not sure whether this would be required.

    A student objects that differentiating the level of responsibility based on the credibility and reputation of the company seems a little unfair.     That's a really fair point. The fact that a company has been operating for a number of years with a good track record may just be luck, and it may not reflect its actual data security capabilities. I suppose this is a kind of rule of thumb that can be applied when deciding whether supervision is required. Of course, you can't just rely on credibility, because you also need to put in place your own security arrangements and get the intermediary to agree to them. You can't just say, you handle this, I'm done. In terms of whether supervision is required, think about the big data intermediaries: Microsoft, Google. In those cases, you probably would not even bother to ask whether you should supervise their data processing, because you're fairly confident these entities are so reputable that they have security processes, and probably better processes than yours.     一位同学提出异议：根据公司的信誉和声誉来区分责任程度，似乎有点不公平。即使一家公司有百分之百的良好记录，错误仍然可能发生，所以责任依然存在。这感觉带有歧视性，因为它取决于公司的地位。

    这是一个非常合理的观点。一家公司多年经营、记录良好，可能只是运气好，未必反映其真实的数据安全能力。我想这算是判断是否需要监督时可以使用的一种经验法则。当然，你不能只依赖信誉，因为你还需要制定自己的安全安排，并让中介同意遵守。你不能只说"你来处理吧，我不管了"。至于是否需要监督，想想那些大型数据中介：微软、谷歌。在这些情况下，你可能根本不会去考虑是否要监督他们的数据处理，因为你相当确信这些机构信誉卓著，有自己的安全流程，而且很可能比你的流程更好。所以从这个意义上说，声誉可以作为判断是否需要监督的一种参考。

  - [19:52:18–19:55:11] **Core Technical Measures: Genki Sushi (2019)**

    So that takes us away from administrative measures and towards the more technical measures. I'll start by mentioning very briefly what the PDPC considers to be the core technical measures: firewalls, security reviews, and patching. As long as your IT system contains personal data, you have to do these things.

    The example case is Genki Sushi, which runs a chain of sushi restaurants. Genki Sushi used an off-the-shelf payroll application, which included a web portal that allowed employees to look at their own payroll information. The application also had a database to store all this payroll information, and the database was hosted on Genki Sushi's own server. Subsequently, they realised their server had been subject to a ransomware attack, and their personal data was encrypted.

    The PDPC highlighted a number of failings. First, Genki Sushi initially did not even have a firewall, meaning they didn't have a filter to control the traffic in and out of the server. And even after they installed the firewall, they didn't properly configure it to do the job. Second, they did not conduct periodic security testing or penetration testing. One of the things an organisation should do is test the system for vulnerabilities, and once you find them, fix them. Finally, they did not ensure their systems were regularly patched. If you use any software produced by someone else, you receive regular patches, and as long as the software continues to be supported, you're expected to patch regularly when updates come. So that's all you need to know as far as the core technical measures are concerned.

    这样我们就从行政措施转向更技术性的措施。我先简要提一下 PDPC 认为的核心技术措施：防火墙、安全审查和打补丁。只要你的 IT 系统包含个人数据，你就必须做这些事。

    示例案例是 Genki Sushi（元气寿司），经营一家寿司连锁店。元气寿司使用了一款现成的薪资应用，其中包括一个网页门户，让员工查看自己的薪资信息。该应用还有一个数据库，存储所有薪资信息，数据库托管在元气寿司自己的服务器上。后来，他们发现服务器遭到勒索软件攻击，个人数据被加密了。

    PDPC 指出了多项缺陷。第一，元气寿司起初甚至没有防火墙，也就是说，没有过滤器来控制进出服务器的流量。即使后来装了防火墙，也没有正确配置使其发挥作用。第二，他们没有进行定期的安全测试或渗透测试。组织应做的事情之一，就是测试系统是否存在漏洞，一旦发现就修复。最后，他们没有确保系统定期打补丁。如果你使用别人开发的软件，你会定期收到补丁，只要软件仍在支持期内，你就应在更新发布时定期打补丁。所以关于核心技术措施，你需要知道的就这些。

  - [19:55:11–19:57:50] **Account Management: Removing Unneeded Accounts — Ascentis (2023)**

    The next technical measure is what's known as account management. For most organisations, if you have an IT system, you create accounts for your users to access it, which of course allows them to access whatever personal data is in the system. If you have that arrangement, you are expected to engage in account management, and there are a few requirements, all of which are pretty obvious.

    The first is that once the account holder ceases to work with the organisation, you should delete or disable the account, to get rid of any unwanted or unnecessary accounts that could create a way in for a hacker. One example illustrating this is Ascentis. The organisation provided CRM software and was engaged by Starbucks to develop and host the CRM system for its rewards programme. Customers who signed up provided their details, and all these details were stored in the organisation's cloud database. Later, Starbucks engaged the organisation for a different project. The organisation then subcontracted a Vietnamese company called Kyanon, and gave Kyanon's employees accounts so they could access this customer data. What happened was that one of the Kyanon employees quit, but his account was not disabled. I think they were quite happy to allow the other Kyanon employees to just reuse the account instead of having to delete it and create new ones. But this was a mistake, because subsequently a malicious actor used that account to access the customer data. In this case, the PDPC said it was a breach of the Protection Obligation not to remove the old account. Organisations have to review their user accounts and get rid of those that are no longer required.

    下一项技术措施是所谓的账户管理。对大多数组织来说，如果你有 IT 系统，你会为用户创建账户来访问它，这当然也让他们能够访问系统中的个人数据。如果你有这种安排，你就需要进行账户管理，这里有几项要求，都相当显而易见。

    第一，一旦账户持有人不再为该组织工作，你就应当删除或停用该账户，清除任何不需要或多余的账户，以免为黑客提供入口。说明这一点的一个例子是 Ascentis 案。该组织提供 CRM 软件，受星巴克委托开发并托管其奖励计划的 CRM 系统。注册的客户提供了个人信息，所有这些信息都存储在该组织的云数据库中。后来，星巴克又委托该组织做另一个项目。该组织随后将工作分包给一家越南公司 Kyanon，并给 Kyanon 的员工开设账户，让他们访问这些客户数据。结果，Kyanon 的一名员工离职了，但他的账户没有被停用。我想他们很乐意让 Kyanon 的其他员工直接沿用这个账户，而不必删除再新建。但这是个错误，因为后来有恶意行为者利用这个账户访问了客户数据。在这个案例中，PDPC 认定没有删除旧账户构成违反保护义务。组织必须审查其用户账户，清除那些不再需要的账户。

  - [19:57:50–20:00:18] **Account Management: No Shared Accounts — Orchard Turn Developments (2017)**

    Another account management measure, which I think was mentioned earlier, is that you should generally avoid having multiple people share the same account. If you have different users who need access to your IT system, each user should have a separate account. The case illustrating this is Orchard Turn Developments. The organisation manages ION Orchard, the shopping centre on Orchard Road. It operated a loyalty programme: if you spend money at ION Orchard, you get points. This programme ran on their loyalty management system, which was made up of a number of servers. One server, called the LMS server, was used to store the members' personal data. A different server, the EDM server, was used to send out emails to the members. In this case, an attacker managed to gain access to the EDM server and then used it to start sending phishing emails to members of the loyalty programme. The most likely reason the attacker got access was that they managed to get the credentials for the admin account.

    The PDPC investigated and found a breach. There were a few different failings on the part of Orchard Turn. One of them was that the organisation created one admin account for four different users. They all shared the same account, same password, everything. The PDPC's criticism of this practice was that with a shared account, you increase the risk of a data breach, because now you cannot tell which user is accessing your server, and you cannot tell who leaked or accidentally leaked their credentials, and so on. You just make accountability more difficult.

    另一项账户管理措施，我想之前也提到过，就是一般应避免多人共用同一个账户。如果有不同的用户需要访问你的 IT 系统，每个用户都应有独立账户。说明这一点的案例是 Orchard Turn Developments 案。该组织管理位于乌节路的购物中心 ION Orchard。它经营一个会员积分计划：在 ION Orchard 消费就能获得积分。这个计划运行在他们的会员管理系统上，系统由多台服务器组成。其中一台叫 LMS 服务器，用来存储会员的个人数据。另一台叫 EDM 服务器，用来给会员发送邮件。在这个案例中，一名攻击者成功访问了 EDM 服务器，随后利用它开始向会员发送钓鱼邮件。攻击者得以访问的最可能原因是，他们设法拿到了管理员账户的凭证。

    PDPC 调查后认定存在违规。Orchard Turn 有几项不同的缺陷，其中之一是该组织为四个不同用户只建了一个管理员账户。他们共用同一个账户、同一个密码，什么都一样。PDPC 对这种做法的批评是：使用共享账户会增加数据泄露的风险，因为你无法判断是哪个用户在访问服务器，也无法判断是谁泄露了、或不小心泄露了凭证等等。你只是让问责变得更加困难。

  - [20:00:18–20:02:48] **Account Management: Principle of Least Privilege — RedMart (2022)**

    One more account management arrangement is to adopt the principle of least privilege. This means that when you create an account for a user, you give the account the minimum level of access necessary. So if the user only needs access to one part of the database, only give them access to that part.

    The example here is RedMart, an online grocer. The facts are a bit complicated, but I'll try to simplify them. RedMart stored its customer data on a cloud database. It used an AWS environment for its apps, and this AWS environment contained a Hubot key, which could be used to access the cloud database. In addition, RedMart had a GitHub repository for its code, which stored a Chef key that could be used to access the AWS environment. So from here you can see how the attacker got in. First, the attacker gained access to the GitHub repository by getting hold of a user account. Then they used that account to find the Chef key, used the Chef key to access the AWS environment, found the Hubot key in the AWS environment, and used it to access the cloud database. And that's how the attacker managed to exfiltrate the personal data. In this case, the PDPC found that RedMart had failed because it had created accounts that gave too much access. There were user accounts with access to the Chef and Hubot keys when it was not really necessary, and this allowed the attacker to obtain those keys.

    So that's account management. Any comments or questions?

    还有一项账户管理安排是采用最小权限原则。意思是，当你为用户创建账户时，只授予该账户所需的最低访问权限。所以如果用户只需要访问数据库的某一部分，就只给他们那一部分的访问权限。

    这里的例子是网上杂货商 RedMart。案情有点复杂，我尽量简化。RedMart 把客户数据存储在一个云数据库中。它的应用使用 AWS 环境，这个 AWS 环境里有一把 Hubot 密钥，可以用来访问云数据库。此外，RedMart 还有一个存放代码的 GitHub 仓库，里面存着一把 Chef 密钥，可用来访问 AWS 环境。从这里你就能看出攻击者是怎么进来的。首先，攻击者通过拿到一个用户账户，获得了 GitHub 仓库的访问权。然后用这个账户找到 Chef 密钥，用 Chef 密钥进入 AWS 环境，在 AWS 环境中找到 Hubot 密钥，再用它访问云数据库。攻击者就是这样窃取了个人数据。在这个案例中，PDPC 认定 RedMart 存在缺陷，因为它创建的账户权限过大。有些用户账户在并不真正需要的情况下也能访问 Chef 和 Hubot 密钥，这让攻击者得以拿到这些密钥。

    这就是账户管理。有什么评论或问题吗？

  - [20:13:44–20:17:24] **Password Management Policy: Password Strength and the CSA Password Checker**

    But let's say you do need to authenticate users to control access to an account. What are you expected to do? There are a couple of things. The first is to implement a password management policy, and the point of that policy is to make sure unauthorised persons do not get access to passwords. There are two components of such a policy: first, password strength; second, password hygiene.

    So first, password strength. Most password management policies should include some rules on the strength of the passwords you demand users create. You should be familiar with some of these guidelines. For example, the password should contain a mixture of character types, not just letters or numbers. You should not use a password related to you or the organisation, because it can easily be guessed. You generally should not use a single dictionary word, because any attacker will brute-force that very quickly. Also, not a common phrase. The password should be long enough, which at present is, I think, at least twelve characters, and if you can make it longer, even better. You should also avoid certain common patterns, which will be guessed very quickly. For example, capitalising the first letter is very guessable and doesn't really increase the security of your password. Having a number at the end is also very guessable. Using symbols to replace letters, like changing an "a" to "@", also doesn't help very much. I suspect some of you will be doing some of these things. I'm also doing some of these things, so it's a bit of a shame.

    If you're interested, you can test out your password by going to this web page called the Password Checker, from the government, the CSA. They've quite kindly coded up a password checker. For example, if your password is "password", it takes just a second to crack. You can see how the time changes as you change the password. If you capitalise, or change the "a" to "@", it will take a bit longer, but still not very long. So you can experiment with how adding things increases the difficulty of guessing a password. Feel free to play with it. That's password strength.

    但假设你确实需要对用户进行认证，以控制对账户的访问。你需要做什么？有几件事。第一是实施密码管理政策，这项政策的目的是确保未经授权的人无法获取密码。这类政策有两个组成部分：第一，密码强度；第二，密码卫生（password hygiene）。

    先说密码强度。大多数密码管理政策都应包含一些规则，规定你要求用户设置的密码强度。你们应该熟悉其中一些准则。例如，密码应包含多种字符类型的组合，不只是字母或数字。你不应使用与你本人或组织相关的密码，因为很容易被猜到。一般不应使用单个字典词，因为任何攻击者都能很快暴力破解。也不要用常见短语。密码应该足够长，我记得目前是至少十二个字符，如果能更长就更好。你还应避免某些常见模式，这些会很快被猜到。例如，首字母大写非常容易猜到，并不能真正提高密码的安全性。在末尾加数字也很容易猜到。用符号替换字母，比如把 "a" 换成 "@"，也帮助不大。我猜你们有些人就在这么做。我自己也在做其中一些事，所以有点惭愧。

    如果你有兴趣，可以去这个叫 Password Checker 的网页测试你的密码，是政府网络安全局（CSA）的。他们很贴心地做了一个密码检查器。比如，如果你的密码是 "password"，一秒钟就能破解。你可以看到随着你修改密码，破解时间如何变化。如果你把首字母大写，或者把 "a" 换成 "@"，会稍微久一点，但仍然不会很久。所以你可以试验一下，添加各种东西会如何增加猜出密码的难度。大家可以随便玩玩。这就是密码强度。

  - [20:17:24–20:19:11] **Password Hygiene and the Debate over Periodic Changes**

    The other component is password hygiene, which is a different thing. Password hygiene is about how you actually use a password once you've created it. There are some generally accepted guidelines. I'm sure most of us have broken these at some point. First, use different passwords; don't use the same password for every single thing. Obviously, don't share your password or write it down on paper, or put it on a Post-it on the screen. Don't log into anything when using an unsecured Wi-Fi network, because someone could be watching. Don't enable automatic login; this is probably the case if you're using some sort of tablet. Obviously, if you think your password has been compromised, that someone may have peeked at it, change your password.

    The last one is debatable, in the sense that some people in the security community question whether it makes sense: periodically changing your passwords. The reason it's debatable is human psychology and how humans work. If you tell your staff to change their password every three months, they'll just change the last character. That's how your staff will normally behave. So some people say this actually makes your passwords less secure. But at present, based on the case law, the PDPC does recommend this practice.

    另一个组成部分是密码卫生，这是另一回事。密码卫生是关于你设置密码后实际如何使用它。有一些普遍接受的准则。我相信我们大多数人都曾在某个时候违反过。第一，使用不同的密码，不要所有东西都用同一个密码。显然，不要分享密码，也不要把密码写在纸上，或者贴张便利贴在屏幕上。使用不安全的 Wi-Fi 网络时不要登录任何东西，因为可能有人在监视。不要开启自动登录，如果你用的是某种平板电脑，可能就是这种情况。显然，如果你觉得密码已经泄露，有人可能偷看到了，就要修改密码。

    最后一条是有争议的，因为安全界有些人质疑它是否合理：定期更换密码。之所以有争议，是因为人类心理和人的行为方式。如果你告诉员工每三个月换一次密码，他们只会改一下最后一个字符。员工通常就是这样做的。所以有人说，这实际上让密码更不安全。但目前，根据判例，PDPC 确实推荐这种做法。

    Let me give you a couple of examples of situations where organisations failed to implement a password management policy. One is the Chizzle case, where the organisation launched a mobile app designed to connect learners and teachers for private tuition. It used a MySQL server as part of its IT stack, and used the phpMyAdmin tool to administer the database. An attacker managed to access the database, wiped out everything, and left a ransom note: if you want the data, pay one bitcoin. It was suspected that the attacker brute-forced their way into the database. The PDPC said that the password used for the database, "Ch!zzle@2018", technically followed the password rules but was still very easy to guess. You have the organisation's name with some variation, the exclamation mark replacing the "i", an "@", and a string of numbers. Given enough time, an attacker can guess this.

    Another example is the Law Society. The Law Society, the association that represents lawyers in Singapore, had a server with all the personal data of its members, and used a VPN solution so its staff could work remotely and access it. For accessing the server, the Law Society did implement password complexity rules, plus a three-month password change cycle. An individual managed to get access to one of the admin accounts, got into the server, and executed a ransomware attack. So what went wrong? When the PDPC investigated, they found that the password was also weak: "Welcome2020lawsoc". Again, it's a long password, but still guessable. In addition, although the Law Society imposed a three-month password change cycle, the PDPC found that this password had been used for more than three months, so people were ignoring the password change requirement. What this highlights is that you not only need to have a password policy, you need to enforce it.

    我举几个组织未能落实密码管理政策的例子。一个是 Chizzle 案，该组织推出了一款连接学生和老师进行私人补习的手机应用。它的 IT 技术栈中使用了 MySQL 服务器，并用 phpMyAdmin 工具管理数据库。一名攻击者成功访问了数据库，删除了所有内容，并留下勒索信：想要数据，就付一个比特币。据怀疑，攻击者是通过暴力破解进入数据库的。PDPC 指出，数据库所用的密码 "Ch!zzle@2018" 从技术上符合密码规则，但仍然非常容易猜到。里面有组织名称的变体、用感叹号代替 "i"、一个 "@"，再加一串数字。只要有足够时间，攻击者就能猜出来。

    另一个例子是新加坡律师公会（Law Society）。律师公会是代表新加坡律师的协会，它有一台服务器存储所有会员的个人数据，并使用 VPN 方案让员工可以远程办公访问。在访问服务器方面，律师公会确实实施了密码复杂度规则，外加三个月的密码更换周期。有人成功获取了其中一个管理员账户，进入服务器并实施了勒索软件攻击。那么问题出在哪里？PDPC 调查后发现，密码同样很弱："Welcome2020lawsoc"。同样，这是个长密码，但仍然可猜。此外，尽管律师公会规定了三个月的密码更换周期，PDPC 发现这个密码已经使用了超过三个月，也就是说人们无视了换密码的要求。这说明你不仅需要有密码政策，还需要执行它。

  - [20:22:04–20:24:37] **Multi-Factor Authentication: Definition and Classic Examples**

    So that was the first secure authentication measure, password management. The second is multi-factor authentication, which we sort of talked about just now. In some situations, you are expected to use multi-factor authentication. Multi-factor authentication means that when you authenticate, you demand more than one factor. It makes it more difficult for a hacker to cheat the verification.

    Some classic examples: when you withdraw money from an ATM, you need your card and your PIN. That's two factors: the card is something you have, and the PIN is something you know. Similarly, if you pay with a credit card online, you need the card details, which is something you know, or if you count the card itself, something you have. Plus you need to key in the SMS one-time password, which is based on you having your phone with you, so something you have. Finally, if you enter Singapore through immigration, you need to show your passport, something you have, and you may have to go through some sort of biometric scan, which is something you are. So all these are examples of multi-factor authentication. As far as IT systems are concerned, as mentioned just now, typical MFA combines a password, which is something you know, plus authentication through an app on your phone, which is something you have. For example, if you sign in to some NUS services, you'll be asked to type in your username and password, and then confirm with an OTP. The question, of course, is: under what circumstances are you expected to implement multi-factor authentication? There are two cases to look at.

    这是第一项安全认证措施，密码管理。第二项是多因素认证，我们刚才大致讲过。在某些情况下，你需要使用多因素认证。多因素认证是指在认证时要求不止一个因素。这让黑客更难骗过验证。

    一些经典例子：你在 ATM 取钱时，需要银行卡和 PIN 码。这是两个因素：卡是你拥有的东西，PIN 码是你知道的东西。同样，如果你在网上用信用卡付款，你需要卡的信息，这是你知道的东西，或者如果把卡本身算进去，就是你拥有的东西。另外你还需要输入短信一次性密码，这基于你随身带着手机，所以是你拥有的东西。最后，如果你通过出入境进入新加坡，你需要出示护照，这是你拥有的东西，还可能需要进行某种生物特征扫描，这是你本身的特征。所以这些都是多因素认证的例子。就 IT 系统而言，正如刚才提到的，典型的多因素认证（MFA）结合了密码，也就是你知道的东西，加上通过手机应用进行的认证，也就是你拥有的东西。例如，如果你登录某些 NUS 服务，你会被要求输入用户名和密码，再用一次性密码（OTP）确认。问题当然是：在什么情况下你需要实施多因素认证？有两个案例可以看。

  - [20:24:37–20:27:07] **When MFA Is Expected: National Kidney Foundation (2021)**

    The first is the National Kidney Foundation case. The organisation is a charity that mostly provides kidney dialysis services. One of the employees, Employee A, fell for a phishing scam. The attacker sent him a phishing email, he believed it, and he gave the attacker his account credentials. The attacker used those credentials to log into the account, download all the emails, and use the email account to send more phishing emails. The emails that were downloaded contained personal data, including health, financial, and marital information about the charity's patients.

    In this case, the organisation used Office 365 for its emails, which allowed employees to access their accounts remotely, at home. The organisation did implement the password management measures we discussed, like a password strength policy, and it would actually lock your account if you failed to log in three times, which is quite a strict policy, among other measures. Nevertheless, the PDPC said this was not enough, because it should have considered using 2FA, or multi-factor authentication. In particular, the PDPC looked at the circumstances. This was a case where users could access their accounts remotely, which is riskier than if you can only access the account through your office computer. In addition, the account gave access to sensitive personal data, like health information. In such a case, the organisation should consider implementing 2FA. And it's clear that if the organisation had implemented 2FA, the attacker wouldn't have been able to access the email: they'd have the password, but then they'd get stuck because they don't have Employee A's phone.

    第一个是全国肾脏基金会（National Kidney Foundation）案。该组织是一家主要提供肾透析服务的慈善机构。其中一名员工，员工 A，落入了网络钓鱼骗局。攻击者给他发了一封钓鱼邮件，他信以为真，把账户凭证告诉了攻击者。攻击者用这些凭证登录账户，下载了所有邮件，并利用这个邮箱账户发送更多钓鱼邮件。被下载的邮件含有个人数据，包括该慈善机构病人的健康、财务和婚姻信息。

    在这个案例中，该组织使用 Office 365 处理邮件，允许员工在家远程访问账户。该组织确实落实了我们讨论过的密码管理措施，比如密码强度政策，而且登录失败三次就会锁定账户，这是相当严格的政策，还有其他措施。尽管如此，PDPC 认为这还不够，因为它本应考虑使用双因素认证（2FA），即多因素认证。尤其是，PDPC 考察了具体情况。这是一个用户可以远程访问账户的情形，比只能通过办公室电脑访问风险更高。此外，该账户可以访问敏感个人数据，比如健康信息。在这种情况下，组织应考虑实施 2FA。很明显，如果该组织实施了 2FA，攻击者就无法访问邮箱：他们有密码，但会卡住，因为他们没有员工 A 的手机。

  - [20:27:07–20:31:07] **When MFA Is Required: Lovebonito (2022) and the PDPC's Guidance**

    This case was followed by the next one, the Lovebonito case. Lovebonito is a fairly well-known e-commerce platform that sells clothing. Lovebonito used two different systems. One is the Magento CMS, which it used to manage the website; if it wants to change the website, it uses Magento. And to process payments, it used the Adyen payment platform. Unfortunately, the attacker managed to compromise the Magento account, the account that allows them to change the website. What the attacker was suspected of doing was using the account to modify the checkout page. When you buy something and click "buy now", it takes you to the checkout page where you key in your payment details. They modified the checkout page so that when you key in your payment details and click send, the details get sent to the attacker instead of Adyen. So they were harvesting credit card information.

    The PDPC said Lovebonito had breached the Protection Obligation. The first reason is the password: the password for the Magento account was "ilovebonito88", which is again super guessable, and the organisation didn't have any written password management policy to speak of. In addition, the PDPC noted that the Magento software actually came with a 2FA feature available out of the box. This means they could just toggle the 2FA feature on, but the organisation failed to do this. Here, the PDPC decided to give the organisation the benefit of the doubt. It said, okay, fine, we didn't give guidance on this before, so we're not going to hold you accountable for this particular failure.

    The PDPC then went on to say when, in future, it expects organisations to use MFA. There are three pointers. First, in general, if you have an admin account that allows access to sensitive personal data, or to a large volume of personal data, you're expected to use MFA, because if someone manages to access that account, the risks are quite high. It's quite rare for the PDPC to say this. They normally don't say "if you don't do this, it will be a breach". But in this case, they are saying that if you don't have MFA for such accounts, it is automatically a breach of the Protection Obligation, unless you can show some good reason why you didn't use it. The second point the PDPC raised was that if you allow remote access, it's even more important to use MFA, in which case, if you don't use it, you'd better have a very good reason. And finally, if the software you're using conveniently gives you MFA and you just refuse to turn it on, this is an aggravating factor that could lead to a higher penalty if you're caught breaching the Protection Obligation. So that's the current set of rules on MFA. Any questions about secure authentication?

    紧随这个案例的是下一个，Lovebonito 案。Lovebonito 是一个相当知名的服装电商平台。Lovebonito 使用两个不同的系统。一个是 Magento 内容管理系统，用来管理网站；如果想修改网站，就用 Magento。另一个是用于处理付款的 Adyen 支付平台。不幸的是，攻击者成功攻破了 Magento 账户，也就是可以修改网站的那个账户。据怀疑，攻击者利用这个账户篡改了结账页面。你买东西点"立即购买"时，会跳转到结账页面输入付款信息。他们篡改了结账页面，使得你输入付款信息、点击发送时，信息被发给攻击者而不是 Adyen。所以他们在窃取信用卡信息。

  - [20:31:21–20:32:37] **Q&A: Do You Have to Give the PDPC Your Password?**

    A student asks whether, in an investigation, you have to give the PDPC your password, since otherwise how would they find out what it was?

    I don't think you'd need to give the PDPC access to your account, unless there's some particular reason. But if the PDPC is investigating you, they will ask you specifically what password the account was protected by, so you'll need to tell them. If you get investigated, you'll reveal this information. Presumably, you'll have changed the password or deleted the account by then. What I mean is, they'll ask what the password was at the time of the breach. So you should change it after the fact, and then tell them what the original password was. Any other questions?

    一位同学问，在调查中你是否必须把密码交给 PDPC，否则他们怎么知道密码是什么？

    我认为你不需要让 PDPC 访问你的账户，除非有特别的理由。但如果 PDPC 在调查你，他们会具体问你账户是用什么密码保护的，所以你需要告诉他们。如果你被调查，你会透露这一信息。想必到那时你已经改了密码或删除了账户。我的意思是，他们会问事发时的密码是什么。所以你应该事后修改密码，然后告诉他们原来的密码是什么。还有其他问题吗？

  - [20:32:42–20:34:31] **Question 2: Newmind and the POLLY "Human Tutor" Messages**

    Let's round up with one more question, which focuses on what we've talked about regarding technical security measures. Here you have Newmind, a company providing AI-powered tutoring services to primary school students. Newmind launched an app called POLLY, which serves a chatbot. To add value, to make it more useful than your average chatbot, Newmind hired a team of tutors, so that if a student was dissatisfied with POLLY's answers, they could request a manual message, and a tutor would take over and chat with the student. Whenever a tutor sends a manual message, the message is headed with "Human Tutor", which differentiates manual messages from the chatbot's messages. Later on, Newmind receives complaints from parents saying their children are occasionally being sent inappropriate manual messages. Newmind suspects an ex-tutor, who was recently let go for poor performance, may have been involved, because the complaints started shortly after he was let go. So the question is: if you were in Newmind's shoes, what would be three actions you would prioritise taking in this situation? Take about one or two minutes to think about your three actions, and then we can discuss.

    我们再用一道题来收尾，这道题聚焦于我们讲过的技术性安全措施。这里有 Newmind，一家为小学生提供 AI 辅导服务的公司。Newmind 推出了一款叫 POLLY 的应用，提供聊天机器人服务。为了增加价值，让它比一般的聊天机器人更有用，Newmind 聘请了一支导师团队，如果学生对 POLLY 的回答不满意，可以申请"人工消息"，然后由导师接手与学生聊天。每当导师发送人工消息时，消息都会以"Human Tutor（人工导师）"开头，以区分人工消息和聊天机器人的消息。后来，Newmind 收到家长投诉，说他们的孩子偶尔会收到不当的人工消息。Newmind 怀疑一名最近因表现不佳被辞退的前导师可能涉案，因为投诉是在他被辞退后不久开始的。所以问题是：如果你是 Newmind，在这种情况下你会优先采取哪三项行动？花一两分钟想想你的三项行动，然后我们讨论。

  - [20:36:53–20:41:11] **Discussion: Containment, Password Resets, Logs, and Filtering**

    So would anyone like to suggest a priority action?

    A student says the first action would be to contain the harm: check whether the ex-tutor's account is still active, disable it, force password resets, and ensure MFA is applied. Essentially, contain the harm before investigating the details.

    So I think you mentioned one of the obvious first steps you might take here, which is basically to force a password reset for everyone. Your suspicion is that someone's account has been compromised, so the first thing you do is force a password reset.

    Another student raises informing the authorities and suspending users; the contribution is only partly audible.

    Oh yes, we talked about that. Make sure the ex-tutor's account has been properly disabled or deleted. That would be your next priority action.

    A student says the first thing is to look at the system logs. At the moment they only suspect the ex-tutor; it's not confirmed, so you need technical means to confirm whether this account is linked to sending these messages. Second, since it's an AI tool, a filtering system should be in place to prevent inappropriate content from being sent.

    Interesting. I guess from a non-data perspective, one thing you might want is some kind of filtering to make sure tutors don't send inappropriate messages, some sort of automated system.

    Another student says: disable the account if it's still alive; make a policy change on passwords if one isn't already in place; and have a second person review messages before they're sent.

    So, a manual review. That's possible. Again, supervision here is probably not so much a data protection concern; it's more about making sure the messages are appropriate. But it would be something logical to do. And you want to make sure your password management policy is being applied, so after you reset, make sure people follow the password policy. I guess one question I would ask at this point is: do you think this would be a case where MFA would be expected?

    那么有人愿意提出一项优先行动吗？

    一位同学说，第一项行动是控制损害：检查前导师的账户是否仍然有效，将其停用，强制重置密码，并确保启用 MFA。本质上就是先控制损害，再去调查细节。

    我想你提到了这里可能采取的一个显而易见的第一步，基本上就是强制所有人重置密码。你怀疑某人的账户被盗用了，所以首先要做的就是强制重置密码。

    另一位同学提到通知有关部门和暂停用户账户，这部分发言只能部分听清。

    哦对，我们讲过这个。确保前导师的账户已被妥善停用或删除。这会是你的下一项优先行动。

    一位同学说，首先要查看系统日志。目前他们只是怀疑前导师，并未确认，所以需要用技术手段确认这个账户是否与发送这些消息有关。其次，既然这是一个 AI 工具，应该设置过滤系统，防止发送不当内容。

    有意思。我想从非数据的角度来看，你可能需要的一样东西是某种过滤机制，确保导师不会发送不当消息，某种自动化系统。

    另一位同学说：如果账户还有效就停用；如果还没有密码方面的政策，就修改政策；并在消息发送前由第二个人审核。

    所以是人工审核。这是可以的。不过这里的监督可能主要不是数据保护方面的问题，更多是确保消息内容恰当。但这样做是合乎逻辑的。另外你需要确保你的密码管理政策得到执行，所以重置之后，要确保大家遵守密码政策。我想此时我要问的一个问题是：你认为这会是一个应当使用 MFA 的情形吗？

  - [20:41:17–20:44:15] **Discussion: Diagnose First, Collusion, Individual Accounts, and Training**

    A student says that before taking any actions, the first thing would be to diagnose the actual cause. Currently it's only a hypothesis that it's the ex-tutor. We haven't determined how it occurred. Is it someone using the ex-tutor's account, or maybe an existing tutor sharing details with the ex-tutor, maybe under some arrangement where they get paid? If you can't identify where the breach is, you can't address it. And even with two-factor authentication, if they're secretly colluding, MFA wouldn't address the issue.

    To address that point, you'd want to find out whether some user is sharing access with the perpetrator, whoever the perpetrator is. Which of course means that, hopefully, when you set up this service, you didn't have all your tutors share the same "Human Tutor" account. Hopefully each tutor had their own account, which allows you to track which of your tutors might be responsible for granting access. But coming back to the question I was asking: would this situation call for MFA?

    A student says part of what we'd want to achieve is to ensure this kind of culture isn't institutionalised among the tutors. They add that the case isn't very clear on whether the staff knew exactly what counts as an inappropriate message, so at some point training would be needed to clarify that, so the tutors don't, for example, make inappropriate jokes.

    I suppose that if your investigation showed it wasn't an external party but actually one of the current tutors sending these messages, then yes, you'd probably need to make sure they know what is inappropriate.

    Another student suggests requiring an OTP to a company email, or access through a VPN, to access the servers.

    一位同学说，在采取任何行动之前，第一件事是诊断真正的原因。目前说是前导师所为只是一个假设，我们还没确定事情是怎么发生的。是有人在用前导师的账户，还是某个在职导师把信息透露给了前导师，也许是某种收钱的安排？如果你找不到漏洞在哪里，就无法解决它。而且即使有双因素认证，如果他们是在暗中勾结，MFA 也解决不了这个问题。

    针对这一点，你需要查明是否有某个用户在与作恶者共享访问权限，不管作恶者是谁。这当然意味着，希望你在搭建这项服务时，没有让所有导师共用同一个"Human Tutor"账户。希望每位导师都有自己的账户，这样你就能追查是哪位导师可能提供了访问权限。不过回到我刚才问的问题：这种情况需要 MFA 吗？

    一位同学说，我们想要达到的目标之一，是确保这种风气不会在导师中形成常态。他补充说，案例中并不清楚员工是否确切知道什么算不当消息，所以在某个时候需要通过培训来澄清，避免导师比如开不恰当的玩笑。

    我想，如果你的调查显示并不是外部人员，而实际上是某位在职导师在发这些消息，那么是的，你可能需要确保他们知道什么是不恰当的。

    另一位同学建议，访问服务器时要求向公司邮箱发送 OTP，或通过 VPN 访问。

  - [20:44:15–20:47:38] **Discussion: Would MFA Be Expected Here?**

    But do you think this would be a case where you'd be expected to use MFA?

    A student says that, per the Lovebonito guidance, failure to use MFA is automatically a breach, so it already says so.

    Is it, though? I guess when the PDPC said failure to use MFA is automatically a breach, they were talking about certain contexts: admin accounts that hold highly sensitive personal data or large volumes of personal data. In those cases you must use MFA, but not under all circumstances. So I suppose the open question is whether you think MFA here would also be reasonably expected.

    Another student says the tutors in this case can remotely access students' confidential information, as well as directly talk to minors through their accounts, so they should have MFA.

    So again, one justification for why the regulator might expect you to use MFA is that even though you don't fit within that specific rule, the broader idea is that if you have a high-risk situation, where an unauthorised third party getting access to an account can cause harm, that would normally be a situation where MFA is also called for. In this particular scenario, an external intruder accessing a tutor's account exposes the children, since the attacker might convince the children to give them more information. That would be a source of data breach. So possibly in this case, MFA would be justifiable.

    A student with experience from the US adds that something useful to consider is whether remote access is involved. Here, certain people can access remotely, which makes it riskier, compared with, say, a typical office where you need to use a company or school laptop, a specific device, to access the system.

    So as mentioned in the second point of the PDPC's ruling in Lovebonito, if remote access is involved, the expectation of using MFA is high. It would be different if all the users were only allowed to access the POLLY app through some company device.

    但你认为这会是一个应当使用 MFA 的情形吗？

    一位同学说，根据 Lovebonito 案的指引，不使用 MFA 自动构成违规，所以已经有明确说法了。

    是吗？我想 PDPC 说不使用 MFA 自动构成违规时，指的是特定的情境：持有高度敏感个人数据或大量个人数据的管理员账户。在那些情况下你必须使用 MFA，但并非所有情况都如此。所以我想，这里的开放问题是：你是否认为在这个情形中，使用 MFA 也是可以合理期待的？

    另一位同学说，这个案例中的导师可以远程访问学生的机密信息，还能通过账户直接与未成年人交谈，所以应当设置 MFA。

    所以，监管机构可能期望你使用 MFA 的一个理由是，即使你不完全符合那条具体规则，更宽泛的理念是：如果你处于高风险情境中，未经授权的第三方获得账户访问权会造成伤害，那么通常也需要 MFA。在这个具体情景中，外部入侵者进入导师账户会让孩子们暴露在风险中，因为攻击者可能会诱导孩子提供更多信息。这就会成为数据泄露的来源。所以在这个案例中，使用 MFA 可能是合理的。

    一位有美国工作经验的同学补充说，值得考虑的一点是是否涉及远程访问。这里某些人可以远程访问，风险就更高；相比之下，比如在典型的办公室里，你需要用公司或学校的笔记本电脑、某台特定设备才能访问系统。

    正如 PDPC 在 Lovebonito 案裁决的第二点中提到的，如果涉及远程访问，使用 MFA 的期望就很高。如果所有用户都只能通过公司设备访问 POLLY 应用，情况就会不同。

  - [20:47:38–20:49:37] **Wrap-Up: Key Data Protection Responses and Exam Scope**

    So I think those were some of the points you'd want to look out for from a data protection perspective. First, the question of MFA. Second, make sure your tutors each have an individual account, not a shared one. And third, the password reset. I guess these would be the first pieces of your response to this potential incident.

    A student asks whether we should really focus on the data protection aspects only, since one of the first reactions to this question might be about control over the content, and other issues that come up.

    I mean, this question is designed to be a bit broad, but in any exam you'll only have to deal with the data protection aspects, not the operational or overall PR aspects.

    I think I'll end the lesson at this point, unless anyone has any other questions. So for today, we've covered just one obligation, which is the Protection Obligation. See you all next time.

    所以我认为，从数据保护的角度来看，这些是你需要注意的一些要点。第一，MFA 的问题。第二，确保每位导师都有独立账户，而不是共用账户。第三，重置密码。我想这些会是你应对这一潜在事件的首要措施。

    一位同学问，我们是否真的只需关注数据保护方面，因为对这道题的第一反应之一可能是对内容的管控，以及其他随之而来的问题。

    这道题设计得比较宽泛，但在任何考试中，你只需要处理数据保护方面的问题，不涉及运营或整体公关方面。

    我想今天的课就到这里，除非还有人有其他问题。今天我们只讲了一项义务，就是保护义务。下次见。
